speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) whether our brand of collaborative tripartism can be better preserved and promulgated by including it in our National Education curriculum.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: More broadly, students learn how consensus is built when groups with different interests work together to achieve collective goals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: In Character and Citizenship Education lessons, emphasis on values like responsibility and resilience helps us stay economically competitive and build social cohesion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: In Social Studies, students learn how the Government, the community and individuals work together for the common good of society.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: With regard to tertiary education students, when they go on an attachment, is there some form of attachment to organisation that values tripartism, so that they can have first-hand experience of tripartism and how it works?
